then.text: Ten legends, ten Stones. It's a good number. Round, symmetrical, and unlikely to be a coincidence.
Mind the kettle. Elspeth gave it to me. It has a mind of its own.

else.text: Dr Anwen Hughes, Wardstone Lab. And you're the one Elspeth keeps sending postcards about. Come in, mind the cables.
Let me show you what the Enclosure's been building. This is a Wardstone.
She holds up a grey disc. It has a barcode, a small green button and a lot of dust.
Wardstones are binding devices. They listen to a legend's resting place, hum back at it, and ask it, very politely, to be somebody else's property.
It works, in a sense, if you're a dragon with no friends. It doesn't, if you have ten Stones that answer to ten legends.
Each Keeper holds a Stone. Each Stone belongs to one old place, and one old story. The legends listen to the Stones, not to the Wardstones.
Which is why the Enclosure wants the Keepers out of the way. And why Pryce went up Yr Wyddfa with a drill.
I'm told the summit did not go to plan. Nothing in the manual about 'the mountain wakes up and shouts'.
Carry on south. The Storm Stone is in Cardiff. When you have it, Dinas Emrys will be ready to see you. I suspect she'll be quite civil. For a dragon.

postgrad.text: I measure how loudly stones hum. It's a very small and very nerdy field.
The hum goes up when a Warden walks by. I've a graph. The graph is rude.

technician.text: Dr Hughes used to share an office with Professor Garside at university. They argued about everything.
They still do, on the phone, for hours. We take bets on who hangs up first.

guild_naturalists.text: Garside's lot write everything down. We just do it in better handwriting.
